title: Closing Time
excerpt: The kitchen closes at midnight. Everything else opens.
content:
The rule was written on the first day, in her own handwriting, taped above the pass: no dating coworkers.

Naomi wrote it after the last disaster, and for two years it worked, because the kitchen was a machine and machines do not flirt. Then Devraj started on floor, and the machine learned to hum.

He was a sommelier with patient hands and a habit of arriving exactly when her station caught fire — figuratively, mostly. He held out water she hadn't asked for. He learned her order at the noodle place downstairs. He never once mentioned the rule.

That was the problem. He never once mentioned the rule.

At midnight the last cover left, the lights dropped to half, and the kitchen exhaled into that private hour where the day is over and nothing has quite begun. Naomi counted her float. Devraj counted her.

"You're staring," she said.

"I'm inventorying."

"The wine list is that way."

"I know where everything is," he said, and the way he said it made her ears go hot under the pass lights.

She looked at the taped rule. She looked at him. Outside, the street was emptying, and the ovens ticked as they cooled, and somewhere below them the noodle place was pouring its last bowls.

"Shift ends in ten minutes," she said.

"Then I'll wait ten minutes," he said, and leaned against the counter like a man who had every intention of doing exactly that — and of being right about what happens next.
